# Spec: forge-setup
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-09 -->
<!-- Source: board item HEF-22 (owner decision 2026-11-07) -->

## Overview

`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` runs in a person's terminal, outside the sandbox, so it is the one place that can configure
the forge for the workers once: the forge's hosts in `orchestrate.allowed_domains`, the HTTPS push rewrite for an SSH
remote, and a report of the stale `config.lock` a sandboxed session leaves behind. The launcher
(`hooks/session-launch.sh`) then turns a worker outcome whose cause is infrastructure into a `stall` block whose reason
is one fixed, copyable fix line — shown once under **Your move** in the orchestrator's brief, never asked as a
`human:intake` form.

**Incident it answers (2026-11-07):** a build finished green and ended blocked at `git push`. The workers' sandbox had
no `orchestrate.allowed_domains`, the remote was SSH (the sandbox proxy carries HTTPS only), and the fix
(`git config url."https://github.com/".pushInsteadOf git@github.com:`) cannot run from any sandboxed session because
the sandbox mounts `/dev/null` over `.git/config.lock` (leaving a zero-byte lock file on the host). The worker's
`blocked` outcome with `blocked_on: null` became `human:intake` (`hooks/session-launch.sh:372`), and the person was
asked six times before running a `!` command.

## Decisions taken from the code (no clarification needed)

- **D1 — where `allowed_domains` lives.** The launcher reads it from the board config (`cfg` →
  `$CONFIG`, `hooks/session-launch.sh:158,176,267`); setup already resolves that same file as `$BCFG`
  (`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:149`). Setup writes there. That file is tracked in git, so setup says it changed a
  tracked file and that the person commits it.
- **D2 — "unless set".** Key absent → setup writes the forge hosts. Key present (any list, even `[]`) → setup leaves
  it untouched and prints which forge hosts it lacks. A person's list is never rewritten.
- **D3 — forge → hosts table** (setup-owned, never read from the board): `github.com` → `github.com`,
  `api.github.com`; `gitlab.com` → `gitlab.com`; `codeberg.org` → `codeberg.org`; any other host (self-hosted Gitea,
  GitLab, GitHub Enterprise) → that host alone. Every host must pass the launcher's own public-hostname check
  (`hooks/session-launch.sh:274-282`); a remote on an IP literal, `localhost` or an internal suffix is reported and
  not written.
- **D4 — which remote.** `remote.origin.pushurl`, else `remote.origin.url`; with no `origin`, the only remote; with
  several and no `origin`, setup notes it and configures nothing for the forge. With an external board, the same for
  each repository in the board's `repos` map (setup already reads it, `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:186`).
- **D5 — SSH forms and the rewrite.** `git@<host>:…` → `url."https://<host>/".pushInsteadOf git@<host>:`;
  `ssh://git@<host>/…` → `url."https://<host>/".pushInsteadOf ssh://git@<host>/`; `ssh://` with an explicit port →
  noted, not rewritten (its HTTPS host is unknowable). Written with `git config --add` to the repository's common
  config (it applies to every worktree), only when that exact value is not already present.
- **D6 — the fix text is never worker prose.** The worker reports a cause from a closed enum; the reason line is
  rendered from a table the plugin owns. The only worker-supplied value that may appear in it is a hostname, and only
  after it passes the D3 hostname check. A worker's summary never becomes a copyable command (constitution 3;
  `.claude/rules/llm-security.md`, prompt injection).
- **D7 — "stale" lock.** `<git common dir>/config.lock` that is zero bytes and older than 60 seconds. Setup never
  deletes it (a live git may hold it); it reports the path and the exact `rm` command.
- **D8 — "shown once".** An infrastructure stall gets no step-2 form; the brief's last line is
  `Your move: <fix line>, then say "retry <id>"`. Several items stalled on the same fix share one line that names them
  all. The person's "retry" runs the existing `ledger.sh unblock <id>` (an ask rule: its dialog is the consent).
- **D9 — api.github.com (owner, 2026-11-09; see Clarifications).** Setup writes it, and the workers reach it: the
  fence is the worker tool allowlist (the default `allowed_tools.implement` — file tools, `Bash(git *)`,
  `Bash(gh pr create *)`, `Bash(gh pr view *)` — with unmatched commands denied), lane-guard and `ledger.sh`'s
  refusal of a worker's unblock, not the network (plan P4 has the exact fence and its config dependence). The lanes' own `sandbox.network.deniedDomains: api.github.com`
  (`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:173`) stays for the lanes; the worker's sandbox is the launcher's `--settings`
  (`hooks/session-launch.sh:294`) in a worktree with no `settings.local.json`. A live check confirms a worker reaches
  `api.github.com` (the deny is gone for it) and `github.com`.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Setup writes the forge's hosts for the workers [P1]
- **Given** a project whose `origin` is `git@github.com:o/r.git` and whose board config has no
  `orchestrate.allowed_domains`
- **When** the person runs `hefesto-setup.sh`
- **Then** the board config holds `"allowed_domains": ["github.com", "api.github.com"]` under `orchestrate`, every
  other key unchanged, and setup prints that it changed a tracked file
- **Edge:** a second run changes nothing and says so; `--print` shows the change and writes nothing
- **Edge:** `origin` on `gitlab.example.org` → `["gitlab.example.org"]`
- **Error:** the key is already `["registry.npmjs.org"]` → the file is not touched; setup prints that `github.com`,
  `api.github.com` are missing from it
- **Error:** `origin` is `git@10.0.0.5:o/r.git` → nothing is written; setup names the host and why
- **Must NOT:** write any host the launcher's check would refuse, or reorder/reformat other config keys

### US2: Setup sets the HTTPS push rewrite for an SSH remote [P1]
- **Given** a project whose `origin` is `git@github.com:o/r.git`
- **When** the person runs `hefesto-setup.sh`
- **Then** `git config --get-all url.https://github.com/.pushinsteadof` in the repository returns `git@github.com:`,
  and setup prints the rewrite it set and that pushes now go over HTTPS (with the credential helper hint
  `gh auth setup-git` when no `credential.helper` applies to `https://github.com`)
- **Edge:** a second run adds no duplicate value; an HTTPS remote gets no rewrite and no message about it
- **Edge:** `ssh://git@github.com/o/r.git` → the `ssh://git@github.com/` form is rewritten
- **Error:** `ssh://git@host:2222/o/r.git` → no rewrite; setup prints why
- **Error:** a stale `config.lock` would block the write → setup stops before writing anything, printing the lock
  path and the `rm` command, and ends non-zero
- **Must NOT:** fetch-side `insteadOf` (only `pushInsteadOf`); touch the global or system git config; act under
  `--print` or `--check`

### US3: `--check` reports a stale `config.lock` and missing forge setup [P1]
- **Given** a zero-byte `<common dir>/config.lock` older than 60 s
- **When** the person (or the session-start hook) runs `hefesto-setup.sh --check`
- **Then** it exits 1 naming the lock path and `rm <path>`, and the lock still exists afterwards
- **Edge:** a non-empty lock, or a zero-byte lock younger than 60 s → not reported
- **Edge:** an SSH remote without the rewrite, or no `allowed_domains` key → reported as missing, with the setup
  command to run
- **Error:** with `allowed_domains` set by the person but lacking forge hosts → reported as a note, not a failure
  (D2: the person's list stands)
- **Must NOT:** delete, create or modify any file or config (`--check` stays read-only)

### US4: An infrastructure outcome is a stall with the fix, not an intake form [P1]
- **Given** an implement (or plan) worker whose structured outcome is `blocked` (or `failed`) with
  `infra_cause: "push-refused"`
- **When** the launcher transcribes it
- **Then** the entry is blocked `stall` with a `reason` that is the fixed fix line for that cause (push-refused on an
  SSH remote → run `bash <clone>/hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` in a terminal; `credential-helper-missing` →
  `gh auth setup-git` in a terminal; `host-denied` with a valid `infra_host` → "the worker reports it was denied
  `<host>` — if the run log confirms the build needs it, add it to `orchestrate.allowed_domains` in `<config>`": the
  host is the worker's claim, never a bare instruction to allow it), the launcher prints that line, and the launcher exits 0 for a `failed` infra outcome
- **Edge:** `host-denied` with an `infra_host` that fails the hostname check → the reason omits the host and says to
  read the run log
- **Edge:** an outcome without `infra_cause` → today's behaviour unchanged (`blocked` + null → `human:intake`,
  `failed` → die, phase kept)
- **Error:** `infra_cause` outside the enum → the outcome fails the schema (as any schema violation does today)
- **Must NOT:** put any part of the worker's `summary` into the reason; replace a `human:*` block (the ledger already
  refuses: `hooks/ledger.sh:562-574`); count as an implement attempt beyond what the claim already counted

### US5: The orchestrator shows the fix once, under Your move [P1]
- **Given** one or more entries blocked `stall` with a `reason`
- **When** the orchestrator writes its brief
- **Then** no step-2 form is asked for them; the status line lists each under "Blocked otherwise" with its reason; the
  last line is `Your move: <fix line>, then say "retry <ids>"` — one line per distinct fix, the one that unblocks most
  first
- **Edge:** a `stall` with no `reason` (the attempts stall, `hooks/ledger.sh:481`) keeps today's Retry/Later form
- **Must NOT:** ask a `human:intake` form for it; repeat the same fix line twice in one brief

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | Setup resolves the forge host of `origin` (D4 rules; `pushurl` before `url`; scp-like, `ssh://` and `https://` forms) and, with an external board, of each `repos` map repository | P1 | US1, US2 |
| FR-002 | Setup maps hosts to `allowed_domains` entries by the D3 table and refuses any host failing the launcher's public-hostname check, naming it | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | Setup writes `orchestrate.allowed_domains` into the board config only when the key is absent and the file is already in `jq .` form (byte-identical), keeping every other key and the file's validity (temp file + `jq -e`); it prints that a tracked file changed. A hand-formatted file is left byte-identical and setup prints the exact snippet and where it goes | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | When the key is present, setup leaves the file byte-identical and prints the forge hosts it lacks | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | For an SSH remote (D5), setup adds `url."https://<host>/".pushInsteadOf <ssh prefix>` to the repository's common config when that value is absent, and prints the rewrite | P1 | US2 |
| FR-006 | Setup prints the `gh auth setup-git` hint when the HTTPS push will have no credential helper (`git config --get-urlmatch credential.helper https://<host>/` empty) | P2 | US2 |
| FR-007 | `--print` reports the forge changes it would make and makes none; `--remove` unsets only the push rewrite values setup recorded it added (`env.HEFESTO_SETUP_EXTRA.push_rewrites`; plan P8), and leaves `allowed_domains` with a note | P2 | US1, US2 |
| FR-008 | `--check` reports `<common dir>/config.lock` (and each `repos` map repository's) when it is zero bytes and older than 60 s, with its path and the `rm` command inside its single `setup: missing …` line (the session-start hook shows only the last line), exiting 1; it never deletes it. The report is meaningful only from an unsandboxed caller (a sandbox mounts `/dev/null` over the lock) | P1 | US3 |
| FR-009 | `--check` reports as missing: an SSH remote without its rewrite, and an absent `allowed_domains` key; a present key lacking forge hosts is a note only | P1 | US3 |
| FR-010 | A stale lock (D7) in a repository that needs the rewrite stops setup before it writes anything ("nothing was written", the lock path and `rm` command); a `git config` write that still fails (a live lock) ends setup non-zero naming what was and was not written | P1 | US2 |
| FR-011 | The implement and plan outcome schemas gain optional `infra_cause` (enum `push-refused`, `host-denied`, `credential-helper-missing`, null) and optional `infra_host` (string, maxLength 253); the worker prompt says when to set them | P1 | US4 |
| FR-012 | The launcher maps a `blocked` or `failed` outcome with an `infra_cause` to `ledger.sh block <id> --kind stall --cause <cause> [--host <h>]`, prints the rendered fix line, and exits 0; without `infra_cause` behaviour is unchanged | P1 | US4 |
| FR-013 | `ledger.sh block --kind stall --cause <c>` validates `<c>` against the enum and `--host` against the public-hostname check, and stores `blocked_on.cause` and `blocked_on.reason` — the reason rendered from the ledger's own fix table (clone path, config path, validated host only) | P1 | US4 |
| FR-014 | `--cause`/`--host` are refused with any kind but `stall`; an invalid host is dropped from the reason, which then points to the run log | P1 | US4 |
| FR-015 | `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`: a `stall` with a `reason` is not asked as a form; the brief names it once and its fix is the **Your move** line (D8); a `stall` without a reason keeps the Retry/Later form | P1 | US5 |
| FR-016 | The worker infra classification never yields `human:intake`: an outcome with `infra_cause` set is a `stall` even when `blocked_on` is null | P1 | US4 |
| FR-017 | `docs/install.md` (setup section) and `docs/hooks.md` describe the forge step, the `--check` lock report and the infra stall | P2 | US1–US5 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Setup on fixture repos (scp SSH, `ssh://`, `ssh://` with port, HTTPS, GitLab self-hosted, IP remote, existing `allowed_domains`) produces exactly the D3/D5 config each time, idempotently | smoke fixtures in a `tests/smoke-*.sh` file, `git config --get-all` and `jq` assertions |
| SC-002 | `--check` exits 1 on a stale zero-byte lock and leaves it in place; exits 0 on a young or non-empty lock | smoke fixture with `touch -t` (POSIX; plan review round 2, #6) |
| SC-003 | A fake worker outcome `{"outcome":"blocked","blocked_on":null,"infra_cause":"push-refused",...}` transcribed via `session-launch.sh … --finish` leaves the entry blocked `stall` with the table reason, never `human:intake` | smoke fixture through the lane `--finish` path (no model) |
| SC-004 | A summary containing a shell command never appears in `blocked_on.reason` | smoke assertion on `ledger.sh show` |
| SC-005 | Each guard is mutation-tested: dropping the "unless set" test, the dedupe of the rewrite, the zero-byte/age test, the infra→stall mapping, the enum check, and the summary exclusion each turn the suite red | `sed` mutants in the smoke file, the pattern of `tests/smoke-lane-cache.sh:116-123` |
| SC-006 | `tests/smoke.sh` tier 1 and `node --test` stay green | run both |

## Clarifications

D1–D8 were decided from the code. D9 went to the owner after plan review round 2 (#4: the worker's cwd has no
`settings.local.json`, so the lanes' `api.github.com` deny likely does not reach a worker).

### Session 2026-11-09 (owner answer, plan review round 2)
- Q: Item 4 / D9 — should the workers reach `api.github.com`? → A: **Allow it; the allowlist is the fence.** Workers
  reach `github.com` and `api.github.com`; a merge stays impossible through the worker tool allowlist
  (`gh pr create` / `gh pr view` only, `hooks/session-launch.sh:200`), lane-guard (`hooks/lane-guard.sh:204-207`) and
  `ledger.sh`'s refusal of a worker's unblock (`hooks/ledger.sh:590,614`). Setup writes the hosts; the live check
  confirms the deny is gone for a worker.
- Q: The other round-2 changes? → A: apply all and re-review until APPROVE (standing decision 2026-11-07, cap 5
  rounds).
